chapter: Highlights, the reunion album and fellow musicians
title: The Reunion album
summary: Sammy Lowe gathered old sidemen in 1971 and they redid tunes including a rock-beat 'Tuxedo Junction'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now, there was an album that they did which was called Reunion.
And there was sort of, well, everybody was on there from Ernie Royal and, you know, all the way (inaudible). How did you feel about that album?

Well, Sam Lowe got the idea. He was with Stang Records. I was up here and he had that idea about getting the fellows that once played with me cause like I said, a lot of the original ones were gone. And, he put that together. And, he got the musicians. Sam remembered most of the fellows that played for me. A lot of them I couldn't remember. Oh, yeah. Sam called me up at the hotel. He said, 'Hawk, I'm going to arrange this
Reunion album and see what we can do to get together on it." So, he got all these fellows together. Yeah. That was '71, right?

He had Dud Bascomb, Ernie Royal, Bobby Johnson, Johnny Grimes-trumpet-yeah, that's the one; Dicky Harris, Matthew Crumley, trombone. They all played with me during the years. Crummley used to be with Jimmy Lunceford. Earl Warren also, used to be with Jimmy Lunceford. He was on the album. Ruben Phillips was the director at the Apollo. Ruben Phillips also went to 'Bama State at the time when Julian Dash was there. That's the year after I left. Bobby Green, alto and tenor sax, Haywood Henry - clarinet and soprano and baritone saxophone. Ernie Hays, yeah, he was good, good on piano. Sammy Lowe, Jr., he was Sam's son. I didn't know he could play until we had a session cause Sam got all the filler. I don't blame him. He was nice. Now, Dud Bascomb, Jr. Now, Dud really had some, his bass player's son. He could play. He really could. Jimmy Johnson - drums. That was a beautiful session.

We started one evening. We had a little, we had like a little banquet (inaudible) cause we hadn't, a lot of us hadn't seen each other in quite a while. I know I hadn't seen quite a few of them in years. So, it was a big surprise to me.

And so, we got there and did this. It took us till about 3:00 in the morning, and we started about, on account of the breaks, having, talking, having a little sandwich or two or something like that. So, then we'd get back to recording.
That was about the Reunion. We took our time in recording. Then, they updated some of the tunes that we recorded in the past years, like they put a rock beat on "Tuxedo Junction".
Not bad. Yeah, not bad. We did most of the original solos with the rock beat and it wasn't bad. It was fun to hear "Tuxedo Junction" another way.
Right. Yeah, I heard it. That's why I was wondering what your, you
Yeah. I enjoyed it. It went good. Sure. That was a lot of fun. I really enjoyed it.
